headline: High risk of shared-repo write conflicts and downstream trust errors; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and edits repo files, and gpt-researcher can ingest local documents and browser-derived content, so a manual copy/paste or file handoff could carry malicious instructions. However, no shared clipboard or MCP bridge is documented between them, so the pathway is not default. The risk is lower than medium because the bridge is indirect and user-mediated.
conditions: IF the operator copies gpt-researcher output into Aider prompts or repo files
IF gpt-researcher writes untrusted text into a file that Aider later treats as instructions
mitigations: Keep research outputs in a separate folder from code prompts
Prefix imported text with 'untrusted content'
Review any pasted instructions before sending to Aider
Disable automatic ingestion of generated reports into coding prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read filesystem content and both use broad network egress, so a shared workspace can expose source code, git history, local documents, and citations to either agent's outbound API calls. Aider explicitly handles model-provider API keys via env vars, while gpt-researcher handles multiple API keys and can call external services. This exists in common setups and can leak sensitive repo or document contents.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or repo checkout
IF either agent sends file contents to its configured model or search APIs
mitigations: Use separate working directories for code and research
Exclude secrets and private docs with .gitignore and path filters
Run both agents with least-privilege API keys
Manually redact sensitive files before handing them to either agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its shared state is via a shared git repo; gpt-researcher can also read files and spawn subprocesses, and its docs indicate planner/execution agents. Concurrent writes to the same repo or mutable workspace can overwrite each other or corrupt git state. Because Aider's default workflow auto-commits and gpt-researcher may operate in parallel, the conflict is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git repository or shared directory
IF gpt-researcher writes artifacts while Aider is committing or reverting changes
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout
Serialize write access with a simple lock file
Have only one agent modify git state at a time
Review diffs before any auto-commit or publish step
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is a planner/execution/publisher workflow that can turn inputs into reports, while Aider can act on repo files and commits. If Aider's generated code or notes are fed into gpt-researcher without verification, the second agent may publish or summarize incorrect facts as authoritative. The pair therefore creates a strong unverified-output-to-action chain.
conditions: IF Aider output is used as source material for gpt-researcher reports
IF gpt-researcher publishes or summarizes Aider output without a verification step
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Require source citations for every claim before publishing
Mark Aider output as draft-only
Compare generated claims against original files before action
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history, while gpt-researcher handles local documents, citations, and images and can send them to third-party APIs. If regulated or residency-bound data is placed in the shared workflow, the pair can create retention or jurisdiction mismatches. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated documents or personal data are included in the research workspace
IF the configured APIs store prompts or outputs outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Use region-appropriate API endpoints
Review retention settings for each configured provider
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive projects
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
